+                if missing:
+                    sep = chr(steps[-1][2] + 1 if steps else 256)
+                    s = sep.join([ch.encode("utf-8").decode("latin-1") for ch in missing])
+                    for pair, new, _ in steps:
+                        s = s.replace(pair, new)
+                    for ch, piece in zip(missing, s.split(sep)):
+                        piece_of[ch] = [ord(c) for c in piece]
+                ids = []
+                extend = ids.extend
+                for ch in text_chunks:
+                    extend(piece_of[ch])
+                return ids

actions.reason: RegexTokenizer.encode_ordinary now stores cached encoded chunks as token-id lists instead of encoded strings. Repeated chunks can be extended directly into the result, avoiding repeated ord conversion over the joined encoded text while preserving the same token sequence.

                     s = sep.join([ch.encode("utf-8").decode("latin-1") for ch in missing])
                     for pair, new, _ in steps:
                         s = s.replace(pair, new)
-                    piece_of.update(zip(missing, s.split(sep)))
-                return list(map(ord, "".join(map(piece_of.__getitem__, text_chunks))))
+                    for ch, piece in zip(missing, s.split(sep)):
+                        piece_of[ch] = [ord(c) for c in piece]
+                ids = []
+                extend = ids.extend
+                for ch in text_chunks:
+                    extend(piece_of[ch])
+                return ids
         # all chunks of text are encoded separately, then results are joined
         ids = []
